The actions described in the paragraph do not appear to violate legal standards regarding working hours, as the employees were already working the maximum hours permitted by local labor laws. Extending working hours without additional pay is not inherently illegal if the total hours do not exceed the legal maximum and if the employees are compensated at least at the minimum wage for all hours worked, though specific overtime laws would need to be checked to ensure no overtime premiums were due for hours worked beyond a standard workweek or day, depending on the jurisdiction. However, the text states they were already at the maximum permitted hours, implying no further hours were added beyond the legal limit, so the extension likely refers to the store's operating hours, not necessarily adding more hours to the employees' existing maximum. If the store simply stayed open longer but employees worked their usual maximum shift, and were paid their regular rate, this is generally compliant. The key is whether "extending working hours" means employees worked more than their legal maximum (which the text says they were already at, so this is contradictory or implies the store hours changed but employee hours did not increase beyond the cap). Given the phrasing "without increasing pay," if employees worked the same hours, pay shouldn't need to increase. If they worked more hours, it would violate the "maximum hours permitted" clause. The most logical reading is that the store stayed open later, but employees worked their standard maximum shift, so no legal violation is evident from the text provided.
